title: Evidence Synthesis
text: Open tooling

title: Evidence Synthesis
text:
The moddafricaes package
moddafricaes — MoDD Africa Evidence Synthesis — is the unit’s R package for collating, analysing and communicating evidence. Its first end-to-end pipeline turns ERA5-Land climate reanalysis into analysis-ready data: derive a study-area bounding box from a shapefile, download hourly NetCDFs from the Copernicus Climate Data Store (CDS), and transform them into Parquet (hourly or monthly) or GeoTIFF (monthly minimum / maximum temperature).
The source lives on GitHub: github.com/modd-africa/moddafricaes.

Install
# pak (recommended — resolves system dependencies too)
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("modd-africa/moddafricaes")

# or with remotes / devtools
remotes::install_github("modd-africa/moddafricaes")
You will also need a Copernicus CDS account and an API key exported as CDS_API_KEY (see https://cds.climate.copernicus.eu/).


The pipeline

All bounding boxes use Copernicus CDS order c(N, W, S, E) — not sf::st_bbox()’s (xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax).







Function
Stage
Output




get_bounding_box()
Setup
c(N, W, S, E) numeric vector (CDS order)


extract_era5land()
Download
One NetCDF per (year, month)


transform_era5land()
Transform
One Parquet per year (hourly)


transform_era5land_monthly()
Transform
One Parquet (monthly means)


transform_era5land_minmax()
Transform
GeoTIFF stacks of monthly 2 m-temperature min / max





End to end
library(moddafricaes)

# 1. Derive a bounding box from a shapefile (zipped shapefiles work via /vsizip/)
bbox <- get_bounding_box(
  "/vsizip/utilities/province26.zip/provinces26/Province26.shp"
)

# 2. Download hourly ERA5-Land NetCDFs for the bbox (needs CDS_API_KEY)
extract_era5land(
  bbox       = bbox,
  years      = 2020:2021,
  output_dir = "data/era5land/nc"
)

# 3. Transform hourly NetCDFs into one analysis-ready Parquet per year
transform_era5land(
  input_dir  = "data/era5land/nc",
  output_dir = "data/era5land/parquet",
  dem_tif    = "RDC_Elevation_Complete.tif",
  years      = 2020:2021
)
The hourly transform de-accumulates precipitation and downward shortwave radiation per day, derives wind speed, relative humidity, vapour-pressure deficit and Celsius temperature, and joins DEM-derived elevation onto the ERA5-Land 0.1° grid. Every write step is idempotent: an existing readable output short-circuits the work, while a corrupt one is deleted and regenerated, so re-runs resume cleanly.






Known caveat. Forcing the de-accumulated daily totals to zero at hour 0 is exact only where 00 UTC falls during the night (as in central Africa). For areas where 00 UTC is daylight, real shortwave flux would be silently zeroed at the day boundary — revisit before applying the pipeline elsewhere.

title: Get Involved
text:
Training and capacity building
A core aim of the project is to build a lasting network of African modellers. Hands-on training runs across the hubs in Tanzania, the DRC and Nigeria, pairing early-career researchers with experienced modellers and real decision problems.
Open challenges

title: Get Involved
text:
Hackathons and modelling competitions
The network runs hackathons and modelling competitions — open challenges that grow skills, surface new approaches, and connect modellers across countries and disciplines.
Community

title: Get Involved
text:
A Community of Practice
MoDD Africa contributes to a regional Community of Practice (CoP) in vector epidemiology and modelling, a space to share methods, data and lessons and to keep the ecosystem connected as it grows.
Programmes

title: Get Involved
text:
For national malaria programmes
We work directly with National Malaria Programmes to make sure models answer the questions that matter for control and elimination — and that the outputs are usable where decisions are made.

title: The Project
text: Background

title: The Project
section: Climate and health in a changing Africa
text:
Climate and health in a changing Africa
Africa’s climate is changing rapidly, reshaping where disease vectors live, how abundant they are, and when they peak. That raises the stakes for vector-borne disease control and for the decisions public-health systems must make. The project frames the problem around four priorities:

How effective are health systems at controlling disease?
How adaptable are decision-makers to emerging threats?
How are key vectors distributed, and how does that shift with the seasons?
What optimised interventions, early-warning tools and evidence are needed to respond?

Meeting those needs calls for models that are trustworthy, hold up in the real world, and keep pace with change.
Approach

title: The Project
text:
The ERA modelling architecture
MoDD Africa is built around an Effective, Robust and Adaptable (ERA) approach to modelling:

Effective — methods that produce answers decision-makers can act on.
Robust — results that hold up under real-world uncertainty and incomplete data.
Adaptable — models that evolve as conditions, questions and diseases change.

title: The Project
text:
What we will deliver
Over the four years of the project, MoDD Africa aims to:

Establish modelling hubs in Tanzania, the DRC and Nigeria.
Develop relevant, model-based advisory systems for malaria control.
Share knowledge through inter-hub training, hackathons and modelling competitions, and a Community of Practice in vector epidemiology and modelling.
Form a strong Evidence Synthesis Unit.

While the initial focus is malaria, the approach is designed to extend to other mosquito-borne diseases, such as arboviruses.

title: Hubs & Partners
text: The network

title: Hubs & Partners
text:
Three hubs, one architecture
Each hub builds local modelling capacity while sharing methods, data and lessons across the network. Tanzania coordinates; the DRC and Nigeria anchor the work in different ecological and epidemiological settings.


Tanzania — Ifakara Health Institute
06°48′S · 39°17′E

Coordinating hub
Hosts the project as regional coordinator and main recipient of funds, and leads efforts to establish the modelling hubs and foster regional collaboration and capacity building.



DR Congo — National Institute for Biomedical Research (INRB)
04°19′S · 15°19′E

Leads the DRC hub, extending the modelling work to one of the highest-burden malaria settings on the continent.



Nigeria — Osun State University
07°46′N · 04°34′E

Leads the Nigeria hub, bringing the network into West Africa’s distinct transmission and health-system context.

Collaborators

title: Hubs & Partners
section: Working with the people who decide
text:
Working with the people who decide
The hubs work hand in hand with National Malaria Programmes (NMPs) and research institutions across the three countries and beyond, so that models answer the questions decision-makers actually face. The network is reinforced by a regional Community of Practice in vector epidemiology and modelling, connecting modellers, researchers and decision-makers as the project grows.






Adding a partner or hub lead? This list is a starting point — update the hub blocks and collaborators as the network formalises.

    The challenge

Control programmes need to see those changes coming, not read them after the fact. MoDD Africa builds the models, evidence and forecasting tools that let decision-makers act early and adapt as conditions change.
